dedupe_keys.name: adaptation pathways for infrastructure operators and policymakers four uk examples university of birmingham 2021

description: This University of Birmingham report explains adaptation pathways, sequences of actions implemented progressively as the future unfolds, for infrastructure owners, operators and policymakers, and compares four UK examples. Emma Ferranti, Sarah Greenham and Ruth Wood wrote it in 2021. The examples are the Thames Estuary 2100 project, which pioneered pathways for flood risk to London with high-end sea level rise scenarios; a Rapid Adaptation Pathways Assessment for coastal erosion and flooding in Somerset built in a 2019 workshop with operators, the council, the Environment Agency and others; and two approaches to managing London's water resources, including the Thames Water resource management plan. It also lists frameworks and resources for building pathways and discusses thresholds and tipping points. Coverage is the UK. Format and access: a 21-page PDF from the university repository. Licence: all rights reserved; free to read. Caveats: it is a synthesis of published examples, and it notes that evidence of effectiveness is limited and that no worked approach exists yet for operators with many asset types such as Network Rail. It supports climate adaptation and capacity planning for infrastructure operators. A related catalogue record is the Thames Estuary 2100 adaptive plan.
